question: After a misconfigured SCCM connector ran for a week, a manufacturer has about 6,000 duplicate Windows servers grouped into 2,100 open de-duplication tasks. The CMDB manager wants them fixed by script, not by hand: keep the CI that Discovery created as the main CI, merge relationships, re-point incidents and changes to the main CI, delete the duplicates, and be able to stop the run if something looks wrong. Question: Design the remediation with sn_cmdb.DuplicateTemplate, covering the template lifecycle, how you would test it, the traps in the options, and how you stop it happening again.
answer:
What the Interviewer Wants to Hear

Walk through the lifecycle the reference lays out (draft, publish, run, cancel, unpublish, retire), test with previewTemplate() and a single remediateTask() before a bulk runTemplate(), and show you understand the selection and merge options well enough to see where they surprise people. Then fix the cause: templates clean up, but they do not prevent.

The Answer

Access. The API is in sn_cmdb and requires the cmdb_dedup_admin role.

1. Create a draft. createTemplate(template) returns the sys_id in reconcile_duplicate_template.

var tplId = sn_cmdb.DuplicateTemplate.createTemplate({
  name: 'SCCM incident Oct-2026 - Windows',
  table: 'cmdb_ci_win_server',
  master_ci_option: 'conditional',
  master_ci_condition: 'discovery_source=ServiceNow',   // evaluated on the template table
  allow_null_attribute_update: false,                     // never copy nulls onto the main CI
  merge_relations: 'all',
  merge_related_items: 'all_available',                  // default entries + any table referencing the duplicates
  duplicate_ci_action: 'delete',
  task_conditions: 'category=attribute^key=serial_number'  // on reconcile_duplicate_task_data
});

2. Check scope. canAddTasksToTemplate(taskIds, tplId) returns success, failed and skipped; skipped tasks have no matching template class (for example Linux servers caught in the same incident). Those need their own template.

3. Preview. previewTemplate(tplId, taskId) works on a draft and validates the required attributes (duplicate_ci_action, master_ci_option, merge_related_items, merge_relations, name, table). It returns masterCI, allClassCIMap, resolvedFieldCIMap (which attribute comes from which CI), relatedTablesMerged and tooManyDuplicates. Preview twenty tasks of different shapes and have the CMDB manager sign off on the chosen main CIs.

4. Publish and try one. publishTemplate() returns true or false. Then remediateTask(tplId, taskId) on a single task; it returns the sys_id of the cmdb_duplicate_ci_remediation record. Inspect the result in the CMDB before going wide.

5. Run and monitor. runTemplate(tplId) schedules a run and returns the reconcile_duplicate_template_run sys_id. Only one run can be scheduled at a time. To stop, requestCancellation(runId) moves it to Cancel Requested; tasks already running finish, and the remaining staged tasks become cancelled.

6. Retire. To change the template, unPublishTemplate() (fails while running or scheduled), then updateTemplate(), which only applies in draft. When done, retireTemplate(), which throws if the template is still published or running.

Edge Cases and Gotchas

  • Main CI fallback. With conditional, "if multiple CIs or no CIs match the query, the method selects the most recently updated CI". In this incident the SCCM duplicates are the most recently updated records, so any task where both or neither CI match discovery_source=ServiceNow silently keeps an SCCM CI. Preview exactly those tasks.
  • Related items condition is evaluated on the selected main CI, not on the incident or change. If it is false for the main CI, none of that related table is merged, which leaves incidents pointing at a deleted CI. That is why the draft above uses all_available; use conditional only when you can state the condition in terms of the main CI.
  • Nulls. allow_null_attribute_update true lets a duplicate's empty field overwrite a populated one on the main CI. allow_master_ci_null_update true restricts updates to fields that are null on the main CI.
  • Large tasks. tooManyDuplicates is true when a task exceeds glide.duplicate_ci_remediator.max.cis (default 1000). Treat those as a different problem (usually a bad identifier), not something to merge.
  • task_conditions narrows which tasks are considered, but the reference warns that a task returned by the query is not guaranteed to be processed.
  • The reference is inconsistent about option names: the list for master_ci_option says newest_created while the update example uses newest_updated. Read the template back with getTemplate() and confirm what was stored before publishing.

Common Mistakes

  • Running the template first and previewing afterwards.
  • Choosing duplicate_ci_action: 'delete' before confirming related items move, which orphans incident history.
  • Cleaning up and leaving the connector as it was. Fix the source's identification (serial lookups, source native keys through IRE), then use IdentificationEngine.runIdentificationAudit(gr) on independent CIs to raise tasks for anything that slipped through.
Score points: Point out the "most recently updated" fallback and explain why it picks the wrong CI in exactly this incident. It shows you read the options as behaviour, not as form fields.

Likely Follow-ups

  • How do you make a CMDB group of the remediated CIs for reporting? (sn_cmdbgroup.CMDBGroupAPI.setManualCIList().)
  • What would you do with tasks where tooManyDuplicates is true?
  • When would you choose duplicate_ci_action: 'update' over delete?

Sources

  • DuplicateTemplate API reference
  • IdentificationEngine API reference
  • CMDBGroupAPI reference

question: A cloud-hosting provider has written its own inventory collector, which pushes Linux servers, their network adapters and serial numbers, and the switch each server connects to. The first version used POST /api/now/table/cmdb_ci_linux_server and cmdb_rel_ci, and within a month there were 3,100 duplicate servers next to the ones Discovery creates. The CMDB owner has banned Table API writes to cmdb_ci*. Compare the Identification and Reconciliation API, the CMDB Instance API and the Table API for this feed, then design the payload and rollout, including how you would test it without polluting production.
answer:
What the Interviewer Wants to Hear

Explain that the Table API inserts blindly while IRE identifies before it writes, then build a proper IRE payload with items, lookup, relations, sys_object_source_info and sysparm_data_source. You should also know about the /query dry run, how to read operation and identificationAttempts, and where the CMDB Instance API fits and where it does not.

The Answer

Why the duplicates happened. POST /now/table/{table} inserts one record and has no idea that a server with the same serial number already exists. Every collector cycle that could not find a sys_id created a new CI next to the Discovery-created one.

Comparing the three.

  • Table API. Generic CRUD. No identification, no reconciliation, no data-source precedence. Fine for reading CMDB data; wrong for feeding it.
  • CMDB Instance API (/now/cmdb/instance/{className}). It is CMDB-aware: source is required and must be a discovery_source choice, it can create inbound and outbound relations with the CI, and GET returns attributes with relations. But it handles one record at a time, needs the itil role, and if the class has a dependent identification rule the payload must contain the sys_id of an existing CI. That makes it a good fit for small, targeted edits from a known sys_id, and a poor fit for bulk inventory where you do not know the sys_ids.
  • Identification and Reconciliation API (/now/identifyreconcile). It runs the IRE on the payload, and the reference says plainly: "Use this API instead of updating the CMDB directly." It handles many items and their relationships in one call and applies identification rules and reconciliation so that only authorized sources update attributes. It requires the itil or asset role.

Designing the payload. I start with GET /api/now/cmdb/meta/cmdb_ci_linux_server, whose identification_rules show the identifiers and their order: on hardware, a cmdb_serial_number lookup on serial_number,serial_number_type, then serial_number, and so on. The payload must carry those attributes or the attempts come back SKIPPED.

POST /api/now/identifyreconcile?sysparm_data_source=TelInventory
{
 "items": [
  {"className": "cmdb_ci_linux_server", "internal_id": "srv-lnx101",
   "sys_object_source_info": {"source_name": "TelInventory", "source_feed": "dc-ams",
     "source_native_key": "node-88231", "source_recency_timestamp": "2026-10-23 01:12:00"},
   "values": {"name": "lnx101", "host_name": "lnx101.tel.net", "ip_address": "10.11.12.173",
              "os_name": "Linux Red Hat"},
   "lookup": [
     {"className": "cmdb_serial_number", "internal_id": "sn-1",
      "values": {"serial_number": "VMW-56 4d 2a", "serial_number_type": "uuid", "valid": "true"}},
     {"className": "cmdb_ci_network_adapter", "internal_id": "nic-1",
      "values": {"name": "eth0", "ip_address": "10.11.12.173", "mac_address": "00:55:51:21:26:2f"}}]},
  {"className": "cmdb_ci_ip_switch", "internal_id": "sw-ams-3",
   "values": {"name": "AMS-SW-3", "serial_number": "Switch23587", "serial_number_type": "uuid"}}
 ],
 "relations": [{"parent_id": "srv-lnx101", "child_id": "sw-ams-3", "type": "IP Connection::IP Connection"}]
}

TelInventory must first exist as a choice on cmdb_ci.discovery_source. Without sysparm_data_source, the reference says the payload goes to the incomplete payloads table. source_native_key carries the collector's own id. Relations can use the parent/child index form, but only between top-level items. The parent_id/child_id form works with any internal_id and survives reordering, so I use it.

Rollout. First, run the whole feed through POST /now/identifyreconcile/query, which determines the insert or update operation without committing. Read result.items[].operation and identificationAttempts[].attemptResult. A healthy run against a Discovery-populated CMDB is mostly UPDATE and NO_CHANGE. A wall of INSERT means the identifiers are not matching. Second, set up reconciliation rules so Discovery stays authoritative for the attributes it owns. Third, commit to production in small batches, log result.logContextId per call, and alert on any MULTI_MATCH, which means duplicates already exist and the 3,100 bad CIs need cleanup before the feed runs freely.

Edge Cases and Gotchas

  • MULTI_MATCH is an identification failure. IRE will not pick one of two candidates for you.
  • values reference fields require sys_ids. Use referenceItems to tie a reference between two items in the same payload instead of looking up sys_ids first.
  • sysId comes back as Unknown when identification fails. Check errors, not just the HTTP 200.
  • Class changes are possible: UPDATE_WITH_UPGRADE, UPDATE_WITH_DOWNGRADE and UPDATE_WITH_SWITCH. Use settings.updateWithoutUpgrade, updateWithoutDowngrade or updateWithoutSwitch if the collector's class detection is less reliable than Discovery's.
  • The relation type must be a name value from cmdb_rel_type.

Common Mistakes

  • Sending only name and expecting serial-based identifiers to match.
  • Skipping the dry run and discovering identifier gaps in production.
  • Calling IRE per CI when a single payload could carry the server, its lookups and the switch together.
Score points: Use the CMDB Meta API to drive payload design from the class's identification rules, and use /identifyreconcile/query as a CI-safe dry run. Then explain why the CMDB Instance API's single-record, known-sys_id model does not suit bulk feeds.

Likely Follow-ups

  • The collector sometimes sends adapters an hour before the server. How do partial payloads change your design?
  • How would you clean up the 3,100 duplicates before turning the feed on?
  • What would you use if the source were a CSV, not an API? (Import Set with IRE-aware transforms.)

Sources

  • Identification and Reconciliation API (Brazil REST reference)
  • CMDB Instance API (Brazil REST reference)
  • CMDB Meta API (Brazil REST reference)
  • Table API (Brazil REST reference)

question: A security vendor's agent sends endpoint inventory to a manufacturer's CMDB through POST /api/now/identifyreconcile/enhanced. Four tickets are open. (1) Some laptops never appear, yet the call returns 200. (2) A vendor engineer set options=partial_payloads:true,deduplicate_payloads:false to "save CPU", but dedup still seems to happen. (3) A batch of Windows servers was converted to a generic Computer class overnight. (4) Ops wants a per-class count of inserts, updates and errors per call for a dashboard. Take each ticket, tell me what the response would show, and what you would change.
answer:
What the Interviewer Wants to Hear

This is a depth check on the enhanced IRE endpoint: partial and incomplete payloads, the options parameter and its forced dependencies, the reclassification operations and the settings that block them, the info codes for skipped reclassification, and the summary from generate_summary. Debug from the response body instead of guessing.

Diagnosis

Ticket 1: laptops missing despite 200. HTTP 200 only says the payload was processed. The per-item outcome is in result.items[]. The enhanced endpoint adds partial payload handling: when an item has an error or warning, its operation can be INSERT_AS_PARTIAL, which stores it in CMDB IRE Partial Payloads [cmdb_ire_partial_payloads] to be merged when the missing data arrives, or INSERT_AS_INCOMPLETE, stored in Incomplete Payloads [cmdb_ire_incomplete_payloads]. I would look at errors, errorCount, identificationAttempts[].attemptResult (likely SKIPPED because a required identifier attribute is missing; a plain NO_MATCH on every identifier would normally lead to an insert, not a missing CI), and sysId, which will be Unknown. One more thing to check: the reference says that if sysparm_data_source is not passed, the payload goes to the incomplete payloads table by default. An agent that forgot the parameter would produce exactly this symptom.

Later, when a follow-up payload completes the item, mergedPayloadIds lists the partial payloads that were merged. That is how you prove the eventual-consistency path works.

Ticket 2: dedup still runs. Documented behaviour: "By default or if partial_payloads is set to true, both partial_commits and deduplicate_payloads are enabled, even if they are set to false, as those features are essential for partial payloads functionality." To turn dedup off you must also turn partial payloads off (partial_payloads:false,deduplicate_payloads:false). Then you lose the merge behaviour that ticket 1 depends on. Leave it on; dedup is not where the CPU goes.

Ticket 3: servers downgraded. The items would show operation: UPDATE_WITH_DOWNGRADE, meaning an existing CI was updated and moved to an ancestor class. The agent reported these hosts with a more generic className than Discovery had. Fixes, in order of preference:

  • Correct the agent's class mapping.
  • Set items[].settings.updateWithoutDowngrade: true for this source. The update proceeds and the class stays put. updateWithoutSwitch and updateWithoutUpgrade do the same for the other two reclassification types.
  • Rely on Reclassification Restriction rules on the instance, and make sure the agent never sends skipReclassificationRestrictionRules: true, which bypasses them.

When reclassification is skipped, result.items[].info carries a code of SKIPPED_CLASS_DOWNGRADE, SKIPPED_CLASS_SWITCH or SKIPPED_CLASS_UPGRADE, a message, and a ruleSysId when a restriction rule caused it. ruleSysId is empty when a payload flag or global flag did. That tells you which control fired.

Ticket 4: per-class counts. Pass generate_summary:true in options. The response then includes a summary object keyed by class, with inserted, updated, unchanged, skipped, partial, incomplete, warnings, errors, additionalInserted and mergedPartialPayloads. Store it per call with logContextId; it is a ready-made feed for the dashboard.

POST /api/now/identifyreconcile/enhanced?sysparm_data_source=SecAgent&options=partial_payloads:true,generate_summary:true
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json

{"items":[{"className":"cmdb_ci_win_server","internal_id":"h1",
  "settings":{"updateWithoutDowngrade":true,"updateWithoutSwitch":true},
  "sys_object_source_info":{"source_name":"SecAgent","source_native_key":"agent-7f21",
    "source_recency_timestamp":"2026-10-23 03:05:11"},
  "values":{"name":"MFG-SQL-04","serial_number":"5CG1234XYZ","serial_number_type":"uuid"}}]}

Edge Cases and Gotchas

  • Use /identifyreconcile/queryEnhanced to rehearse option changes. It simulates the enhanced endpoint without committing.
  • additionalCommittedItems and additionalCommittedRelations list records IRE wrote that were not in your payload. Include them in your audit, or the counts will not reconcile.
  • Relations have their own INSERT_AS_PARTIAL and INSERT_AS_INCOMPLETE outcomes, so a CI can succeed while its dependency relationship parks.
  • source_recency_timestamp must be UTC in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss. An agent sending local time makes stale data look fresh.
  • markers are documented as internal use. Do not build logic on them.

Common Mistakes

  • Alerting on HTTP status instead of errorCount and operation.
  • Turning partial payloads off to "simplify" and then losing every item that arrives before its parent data.
  • Fixing downgrades by editing CI classes manually, which the next agent run reverses.
Score points: Quote the rule that partial_payloads forces partial commits and dedup on, and show how info.ruleSysId separates a restriction rule from a payload flag.

Likely Follow-ups

  • How long should partial payloads be retained before you treat them as data-quality defects?
  • How would you give Discovery precedence over this agent for os_version but not for installed software?
  • What does duplicateLookupIndices tell you about the agent's payload?

Sources

  • Identification and Reconciliation API (Brazil REST reference)

question: A mobile network operator is replacing its legacy fault desk with ServiceNow Telecommunications Service Management. Its OSS (network inventory and alarm platform) and two wholesale partners already speak TM Forum Open APIs. The architecture board wants (1) partners to raise and track trouble tickets through TMF621, (2) the OSS to stream alarms into ServiceNow through TMF688, and (3) partners to receive notifications only for priority-1 incident updates. During the proof of concept: the OSS team says every alarm call returns 200 but some alarms never appear; a partner's tickets all landed as incidents when they should have been cases; tickets created with severity "P1" became Low; and a partner's poller crashed on a 404 when it had no open tickets. Explain each behaviour from the API definitions and design the target integration.
answer:
What the Interviewer Wants to Hear

Explain each surprise from the ServiceNow implementation of the TMF specification instead of blaming the partners. The Trouble Ticket Open API defaults ticketType to Incident, quietly maps invalid severities to Low and invalid statuses to New, returns 404 when a query matches nothing and 206 when a page is partial, and returns only comments (never work notes) in note. The TMF688 event endpoint is asynchronous through NowMQ and returns 200 for every call regardless of outcome. Partner notifications are scoped by registering topics with header and content queries.

The Answer

Trouble tickets (TMF621). POST /api/sn_ind_tsm_core/ticket/troubleTicket requires description, severity and status. ticketType selects the table: Case (sn_customerservice_case), Incident, or Service Problem Case. It defaults to Incident, which is why the partner's tickets landed there. Severity maps to Priority, and you "must provide the choice value only" (1 to 4, plus 5 Planning for incidents). An invalid value becomes Low, so "P1" became Low. Status accepts a label or a value, and an invalid one becomes New. relatedParty fills Contact/Account for cases and Caller/Company for incidents. relatedEntity points to assets, sold products or product inventory for cases, or CIs and services for incidents. note[] entries with @type comments or work_notes go into the matching journal field. Updates use PATCH .../troubleTicket/{id}.

Polling. GET .../troubleTicket filters on ticketType, status, severity and id. limit defaults to 25 with a maximum of 100; both are set by the sn_ind_tsm_sdwan.pagination.set_limit and .max_limit properties. Responses are 200 for a complete result, 206 for a partial page (with Content-Range, Link and X-Total-Count), and 404 when nothing matches. The partner's poller must treat 404 on a list query as "zero tickets", not as a failure.

Alarms (TMF688). The Event Notification Management Open API exposes a single registered endpoint per source (instance name, scope ID, GUID). It puts each payload on a NowMQ queue, and a background process creates, updates or deletes em_event records. The response is 200 for every call and has no body. It "only indicates that the endpoint received the request". The likely cause of the missing alarms is payloads that failed during background processing (for example, missing a field required for that eventType), which a 200 cannot reveal. For create, the required fields are alarmedObject.id, alarmType, externalAlarmId, perceivedSeverity (CLEAR, CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, WARNING), probableCause and sourceSystemId. Payloads are checked against the schemas in the TMFAlarmAPIConstants script include, and unknown fields are dropped. Reconcile by checking em_event and alerts on the instance, not by reading HTTP codes.

Partner notifications. Register a topic with POST /api/sn_api_notif_mgmt/topic (role sn_api_notif_mgmt.event_mgmt_integration), using a headerQuery that selects event types and a contentQuery that filters the payload:

{"name": "PartnerA-P1-Incidents",
 "externalId": "partnerA-p1",
 "namespace": "wholesale",
 "headerQuery": "eventType=TroubleTicketStatusChangeEvent,TroubleTicketAttributeChangeEvent",
 "contentQuery": "troubleTicket.ticketType=incident&troubleTicket.severity=1"}

In these queries, & means AND, commas mean OR, and dotted paths reach into the event object. A duplicate externalId, or a duplicate combination of name, namespace and both queries, returns 400.

Edge Cases and Gotchas

  • The TMF688 page names the event types inconsistently. The overview says AlarmCreateEvent, AlarmUpdateEvent and AlarmDeleteEvent. The eventType parameter lists AlarmCreateNotification, AlarmChangeNotification and AlarmDeleteNotification, and the example uses AlarmCreateNotification. Confirm against TMFAlarmAPIConstants on your instance.
  • Once an alarm is CLEAR, its perceived severity can no longer be set.
  • From the October 2026 Telecom Core store release (v6.7.3), the trouble ticket path moved from /api/app_ind_tsm_sdwan/... to /api/sn_ind_tsm_core/.... Partners hard-coded to the old path need to move.
  • GET returns only customer-visible comments in note, never work notes. Partners won't see internal notes, which is usually what you want, but it surprises people.
  • Case tickets need the Case Management Core and Install Base plugins. The caller needs ticket_integrator.

Common Mistakes

  • Letting partners send TMF severity labels and expecting a mapping. Agree on numeric choice values in the interface contract.
  • Monitoring the alarm integration by HTTP success rate.
  • Building one topic per partner with no content filter and filtering on the partner side.
Score points: Tie each POC symptom to a specific documented default: Incident as default ticketType, Low for invalid severity, 404 for an empty list, 200-always for TMF688. Then propose contract tests that send deliberately wrong values to check those defaults before partners go live.

Likely Follow-ups

  • How would you extend the Trouble Ticket API to require a partner reference field?
  • How do alarms from TMF688 become incidents that partners then see through TMF621?
  • How would you replay alarms after a queue backlog?

Sources

  • Trouble Ticket Open API (Brazil REST reference)
  • Event Notification Management Open API (Brazil REST reference)
  • Event Management Topic Open API (Brazil REST reference)
